title: A3-TTA: Adaptive Anchor Alignment Test-Time Adaptation for Image Segmentation
mechanism: Target images with compact class density act as anchors. Pseudo-labels for the others are built under anchor guidance, regularised by boundary-aware entropy and a self-adaptive EMA.
adaptation: Anchors are E1 cells whose crack/inactive feature density is close to the train prototype (likely the plain full cells). Anchor-guided pseudo-labels then go to half-cut scuff cells. Crack anchors must be class-balanced (BAPA CBA), or background dominates.
min_experiment: Arm: SUP100-PF + A3-TTA on E1 modules. Baseline: SUP100-PF. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gains < +0.02, or test guard drops > 0.005, or H36 crack-free false alarms rise > 2x.
evidence: R: +10.40 to +17.68 Dice over the source model on multi-domain heart and prostate segmentation plus natural images; robust in continual TTA.
prior_overlap: Partial. Pseudo-label SSL with the 11.9k pool was n.d. at 100%, but that used generic pool cells and fixed thresholds during training, not anchor-guided adaptation on target modules.
